experiment.title: the prompt was the wrong primitive
experiment.hook: we built everything on the wrong primitive.
experiment.hypothesis: a thesis-declaration hook ('the prompt was the wrong primitive') + a quotable close beats a problem-first teardown for cold reach on a skeptical AI-infra audience
experiment.caption:
i wrote the cleanest prompt of my life last tuesday. genuinely proud of it. the agent shipped exactly what i wanted and then i closed the tab and it was just... gone. and so i'm sitting there like wait — the thing that knew the goal + the tradeoffs + why we picked postgres over the thing we almost picked, that all lived in a conversation i just deleted. that's when it clicked that the prompt was never the primitive. the conversation can't be the thing that remembers your company, right? the org has to. so orgx passes a compiled handoff instead of a transcript — goal, definition of done, decisions and why, budget, next action — and the work lives in a graph, not a thread that dies when you hit close. the prompt ends. what keeps moving after is the whole point and almost nobody's building for that part yet

#aiagents #aiinfra #multiagent #promptengineering #buildinpublic #agentic #devtools #mcp

slides.headline: we built everything on the wrong primitive.
slides.subtext: and we're all still building on top of it.

slides.headline: you write a perfect prompt. the agent nails it. then the chat closes.
slides.subtext: and everything it knew closes with it.

slides.headline: the goal, the decisions, the why — gone with the transcript.
slides.subtext: the next agent starts from zero. again.

slides.headline: the conversation was never meant to hold your company.
slides.subtext: the org has to remember why the work exists — not the chat.

slides.headline: the handoff gets compiled, not dumped.
the work lives in a graph, not a thread.
the prompt ends. the company keeps moving.
slides.subtext: follow if you're building agents that outlive the chat.
